events.title: OpenAI GPT-4.1 released
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-4.1 on April 14, 2025 — improved coding, instruction following, and a 1M-token context window in the API.
events.about: GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini targeted developers with better long-context coding and lower latency than GPT-4o. The release continued OpenAI's cadence of incremental API models between flagship consumer launches.

narrative.whyChosen: GPT-4.1 pushed long-context coding further in the developer API tier.
narrative.whyImportant: Million-token API models reduced chunking for codebase-aware tools.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers needed stronger coding models with larger context at API scale.

events.title: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini released
events.summary: OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 — reasoning models with tool use, coding, and science benchmarks that replaced o1 in ChatGPT and the API.
events.about: After December's preview, o3 brought private chain-of-thought reasoning to production alongside the smaller o4-mini. Together they anchored OpenAI's reasoning tier until GPT-5 unified fast and thinking modes — and kept pressure on Google Gemini 2.5 and Anthropic Claude 4.

narrative.whyChosen: o3 moved OpenAI's second-generation reasoning models from preview to production.
narrative.whyImportant: Reasoning plus tool use became the default stack for hard coding and research agents.
narrative.problemSolved: o1 users needed stronger STEM, coding, and agentic performance at API scale.

events.title: Meta Llama 4 Scout and Maverick released
events.summary: Meta released Llama 4 Scout and Maverick on April 5, 2025 — open-weight natively multimodal MoE models with up to 10M-token context on Scout.
events.about: Llama 4 brought mixture-of-experts and native multimodality to Meta's open model line. Scout fit on a single H100; Maverick beat GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash on several benchmarks. Meta also previewed the training-only Behemoth teacher — signaling open weights would keep pace with closed frontier models.

narrative.whyChosen: Llama 4 made open MoE multimodal models competitive with closed API flagships.
narrative.whyImportant: Ten-million-token context and MoE efficiency reset expectations for self-hosted AI.
narrative.problemSolved: Open-source teams needed frontier multimodal models without cloud API dependence.

events.title: Alibaba Qwen3 released
events.summary: Alibaba open-weighted Qwen3 on April 28, 2025 — hybrid thinking and non-thinking modes across dense and MoE models up to 235B parameters.
events.about: Qwen3 matched or beat o1, DeepSeek R1, and Gemini 2.5 on several public benchmarks while supporting 119 languages. Hybrid reasoning let developers toggle extended thinking per task — making Alibaba a top-tier open-source alternative alongside DeepSeek and Meta.

narrative.whyChosen: Qwen3 put Alibaba firmly in the open frontier model race with hybrid reasoning.
narrative.whyImportant: Chinese open-weight models became credible defaults for global self-hosted deployments.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams wanted o1-class reasoning with open weights and flexible thinking budgets.
